cadence: weekly, Monday before the US open
method: Every Monday each open call is re-examined against the claims its note made. The numbers are computed from the record: where the call stands against what the note called for, how far the stop is, and a price-only range for where it can finish, drawn from the position's own recent volatility with no view assumed. The verdict is a judgment, stated with dated evidence: each claim the note relied on is re-measured and marked as holding or not, and the verdict has to follow from those marks. A broken thesis closes the call on the Scorecard from the review date. The return a note called for is written once and never changed.

latest.book_now: After this week's review the book holds three calls: long US energy stocks, long the yen and long US natural gas. The S&P 500 put reached its planned close on Wednesday and is off the book. One reason is fully in place and two are weakened; none is broken. The week's story was a hot US inflation report on Nov 10 that sent the 10-year Treasury yield from 4.86% back to 5.15% and the dollar to a 19-month high. That restored the bond-yield half of the energy call, whose fund rose 5.4% to sit level with entry, and it is why that call moves back to intact; we hold the half position and let the exit rule manage it. The same move hurt the yen call: dollar-yen broke out of its eight-week range and touched 160.30, Tokyo answered with words rather than money, and a New York Fed report showed the US share of the summer rescue was far smaller than advertised, so we now expect roughly a break-even finish and hold without adding. The gas call has done what it said in the commodity, with gas at 3.23 against a 3.05 target, and a 9% week brought the fund back to level with entry; with the gap it was built on mostly closed and four weeks left, we take half of what remains off. Energy stocks carry the most conviction this week, the yen the least. A reader holding the calls trims the gas fund today and leaves the energy and yen positions as they are.

book.basis: equal weight across the open calls, one unit each, trailing 63 sessions; a 21-session driftless range

book_risk.note: correlations are of daily mark changes over the trailing 63 sessions; exposure is the position's % move per 1% in equities or the dollar and per +10bp in the 10-year yield

calls.title: Oil carries a war premium. US natural gas carries none.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's base rate: median front-month gas gain over three months after an oil-to-gas ratio reading at or above the 95th percentile (42 episodes since 2004)
calls.expected_basis: gas is already above the note's 3.05 target and the gap is under the line the edge was measured from, so we credit no further gain in gas over the four weeks left; a flat gas price costs the fund a little on the contract roll before Dec 11, so from level with entry we expect a finish about 1% under entry
calls.view_now: The call worked in the commodity: gas is up 15% from entry and through the target, oil is down 11%, and the gap between them has mostly closed, as the note said it would. A cold snap and record export demand lifted gas 8% this week and brought the fund from 8% under entry back to level. From here there is little of the original edge left to collect: the gap is no longer extreme, forecasts turn milder late in the month, and the fund pays for another contract roll before Dec 11. We expect it to finish about where it is, slightly under entry.
calls.action_reason: Take off half of what is left. The gas price has passed the target the note set and this week's rally has returned the fund to level with entry, which is the best exit the fund has offered since October; we keep the other half to the planned close on Dec 11 because the exit level is 24% away, export demand is at a record and funds were still record short in the last report, so a cold December could still pay
calls.weakened_reason: Every line holds, and the thesis is weakened because it has largely been used up rather than because it failed. Gas has passed the note's 3.05 target and the oil-to-gas gap has come in from the 96th to the 87th percentile, well under the line the edge was measured from, so the history behind the call says little about the next four weeks. The fund is only back to level with entry, because the autumn contract rolls cost it roughly what the gas price gained, and another roll falls before the planned close

The gap has closed from both ends as the note said: front-month gas is 3.23, up 15% from the 2.82 at entry and above the note's 3.05 target, and US crude is $88.56, down 11% from entry. The reading is now well below the 95th-percentile line the edge was measured from, so most of the extreme the call rests on is gone

driver_checks.claim: No weekly close in front-month gas below 2.45.
driver_checks.now: 3.23 at Friday's close, after 3.34 on Thursday, the week's high; the exit level is 24% below the market, and a fall of that size over the sessions left has happened about 5% of the time in the series' own history. calls.title: The record yen rescue looks dead. So did the last three at exactly this point.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's target: 147 on dollar-yen by late January 2027, the median months-two-to-six move applied from 157.34, roughly +6% on the fund
calls.expected_basis: three outcomes weighed: about a one-in-two chance that Tokyo acts or the Bank of Japan's December rise turns the yen and the fund finishes about 3% ahead, a shortened version of the three earlier campaigns' median; about a one-in-three chance of a weekly close above 164, which ends the call about 4% under entry; and the rest a flat finish near today's 1.4% under entry. Together about half a per cent ahead, down from 4% a week ago
calls.view_now: The campaign has not been withdrawn, but it is being tested and so far defended only with words. Dollar-yen broke its two-month range on the back of higher US yields and sits at 159.56, inside the 160 to 164 zone where Tokyo spent money in July and August; the note said a push into that zone was expected to draw action, and this week will show whether it does. With 43% of the horizon gone, the yen 1.4% weaker than at entry and the US backing shown to be thin, we no longer expect the 6% the note called for. We see roughly even odds between Tokyo acting and the pattern playing out late, and a weekly close above 164 that ends the call, which nets to about break-even.
calls.action_reason: Leave the position as it is and do not add. The note treated a push into the 160 to 164 zone as the place the authorities act, the campaign has not been withdrawn and a December rate rise in Japan is increasingly expected, so the thesis is not broken; but the US backing has turned out thin and the exit is under 3% away, so the weekly-close rule at 164 decides it from here rather than more of our money
calls.weakened_reason: Every line still holds, but the week moved against the call on two fronts. Price: a hot US inflation report lifted the dollar to a 19-month high and dollar-yen broke out of its eight-week range to 160.30, leaving the exit 2.8% away instead of 4.1%, with the base-rate chance of reaching it up from about 30% to about 44%. The driver itself: Tokyo answered the break with warnings rather than yen buying, and the New York Fed's report showed the US put only about $0.5 billion into the summer campaign, which makes the joint action the note leaned on a weaker deterrent than it looked

driver_checks.claim: An official yen-buying campaign is under way and the authorities have not stepped back from their stated readiness to act.
driver_checks.at_publication: Record 15.4 trillion yen campaign begun Jul 30 with the United States; finance minister pledged further coordinated action on Aug 3
driver_checks.now: No retraction, but words only: on Nov 12 Japan's top currency official said the yen's fall was too rapid and that it was too early to forget the summer, and on Nov 13 the finance minister said one-sided, sharp moves were emerging and Japan would respond appropriately with the US Treasury. No yen buying has been reported since Aug 3. A New York Fed report in the week showed the US share of the summer campaign was about $0.5 billion, far below the up to $10 billion the Treasury Secretary had hinted at. Markets increasingly expect the Bank of Japan to raise its rate in December
driver_checks.source: Reuters, Nov 12-13 (finance minister and currency official remarks; New York Fed report); Seoul Economic Daily, Nov 14

driver_checks.claim: The pattern is a month-two retest followed by the real move in months two to six; this call entered at the retest.
driver_checks.at_publication: Dollar-yen 157.34 on Sep 22, within 2% of the level where the buying began
driver_checks.now: eight weeks in, the move has not started and the retest has gone further: dollar-yen broke above the 156.5 to 158.6 range of the past eight weeks, touched 160.30 on Nov 12, the weakest yen since early September, and closed Friday at 159.56, 1.4% above the level at entry. The campaign is in its fourth month, so the window the pattern allows runs to the end of January and is still open. The fund is 1.4% under entry with 48 sessions to the planned close. Speculators held a long yen position at the 83rd percentile of three years in the latest report, which predates this week's fall

calls.title: Yields and oil are surging together. Energy stocks gained after that in 7 of 8 cases.
calls.called_for_basis: the note's expected return: the average fund return over six months in the eight earlier cases, with the 10% weekly-close exit applied
calls.expected_basis: oil is now in the top fifth of its three-year range rather than the top tenth, and the note's own test of that looser condition gave an average of +5.6% over six months across 12 cases; scaled to the four-fifths of the horizon still ahead that is about +4.5%, less the 0.4% the fund is under entry, for a finish about 4% ahead
calls.view_now: Both halves of the setup are back in place. The bond-yield half, which had handed back more than half of its rise a week ago, was restored by a hot inflation report: the 10-year yield is at 5.15%, within a tenth of a point of where the note was written. Oil slipped another 2.5% but is still at the 85th percentile of three years, and the peace hopes that drove the prior week's fall have faded. The fund rose 5.4% in the week to sit level with entry, with the exit now more than 10% away. We expect the call to finish ahead, though by less than the note called for, because oil is in the top fifth of its range rather than the top tenth the strongest cases had.
calls.action_reason: Hold the half position left after last week's cut and do not rebuild it yet. Every condition holds and the yield half of the setup is restored, but oil is only 6% above the line that would break the call and one headline on Iran can cover that distance; a second week with oil holding above about $83.50 is the case for going back to full size

driver_checks.claim: Oil remains expensive relative to its recent range: US crude in the top fifth of its three-year range.
driver_checks.at_publication: 93rd percentile of three years, $96.24 on Oct 6
driver_checks.now: 85th percentile of three years, $88.56 at Friday's close, down 2.5% in the week after the 13% fall the week before. The line that would undo the call is the 80th percentile, about $83.50, now 6% below the market. Hopes of a negotiated end to the Iran war faded: the President said on Thursday that no deal with Iran is needed, and October saw the most attacks on commercial ships in the Gulf since the war began, with more ships hit this week
driver_checks.source: macrotilt.com indicator history (US crude, West Texas Intermediate); Bloomberg via Rigzone, Nov 13; Reuters via RTE, Nov 13
